articles.title: Ladd McConkey downgraded to out vs. Ravens due to back issue
articles.summary: Ladd McConkey has been limited by multiple injuries this season.
articles.body:
A frustrating season for Los Angeles Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey will continue in Week 10. While the receiver was initially listed as questionable on the team's final injury report, he will not play against the Baltimore Ravens on "Monday Night Football."

McConkey was ruled out for the game due to back spasms. He did not travel with the team to Baltimore, the Chargers announced.

McConkey has been limited by multiple injuries throughout the regular season. He was held to just 35 yards in Week 2 thanks to a rib injury and missed Week 5 due to a foot issue.

He caught just one ball in Week 6 before resting during the bye week. While the wideout looked to be close to 100 percent with an 86-yard performance in Week 8, McConkey missed Week 9 with back spasms. The injury reportedly occurred just before game time. He was expected to play in the contest.

Those back spasms have apparently continued to plague McConkey throughout the week. He was held out of practice each day leading up to Week 10, though the team still held some hope he would play, initially giving him the questionable tag.

But the issue was bad enough that the team opted against throwing McConkey on the field Monday night.

At 0-8, the Chargers are desperate to pick up their first win of the season. That could come in Week 10, as the Ravens will start newly acquired Jacoby Brissett in the contest.

Without McConkey, however, the team will need other receivers like Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris to step up if it hopes to pick up a victory.

articles.title: Jahmyr or JSN: Who's the Offensive Player of the Year in the NFL this season?
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are both making strong cases as the best offensive players in the NFL this season.
articles.body:
Imagine you're an offensive coordinator in the NFL. And, as long as we're in the world of make-believe, imagine you have both Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba on your roster. And imagine you have exactly one play to get into the end zone.

Do you go with the running back who can stomp upstream through rush-hour traffic? Or do you go with the receiver who can create space in a mosh pit? Ground game or air game? Who's your favorite for NFL Offensive Player of the Year?

Sunday served as center stage for both Gibbs and Smith-Njigba, half a world apart. Before half the United States had even woken up, Gibbs began a methodical demolition of New England in Munich, rushing for 153 yards and two touchdowns and receiving another 99 through the air as Detroit won 35-10. A few hours later, Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 171 yards, including a 71-yard beast of a touchdown, as Seattle outlasted Las Vegas 21-13.

Through Week 10, both teams remain in the hunt for playoff berths, in large part because of the outsized, generational performances of their stars.

After three seasons in the backfield alongside David Montgomery as a Sonic-and-Knuckles duo, Gibbs is now a solo act; Detroit thought enough of his potential that the Lions dealt Montgomery to the Texans. Gibbs validated the Lions' trust in him; this season, he leads the NFL in (deep breath) attempts, yards, touchdowns, first downs, rushing yards per game, touches from scrimmage, yards from scrimmage and combined receiving and rushing touchdowns.

Just three-plus seasons into his career, Gibbs is already starting to carve his way into the NFL record books. He just passed Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns through the first four years of a career, with 62. And he joined a couple guys named Emmitt Smith and Barry Sanders as the only players to rush for 50 touchdowns before turning 25.

"I think we have to pinch ourselves sometimes and not take for granted how special he is," Lions quarterback Jared Goff said after Sunday's victory . "He's just so explosive with the ball in his hands. I throw a check-down to him, and he goes for 50 yards. That's so rare for a guy to be able to do all the things he does."

Here, from Sunday, is a perfect encapsulation of everything Gibbs brings to the field: speed, power and a relentless drive into the end zone.

Also in his fourth year, Smith-Njigba is both a defending Super Bowl champion and the defending Offensive Player of the Year. While Seattle is struggling to defend its title, Smith-Njigba is authoring a brilliant sequel to his 2025. He currently leads the league in (another deep breath) receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns, receiving first downs, longest reception, receiving yards per game and yards per touch from scrimmage.

His performance Sunday against the Raiders was nothing short of exceptional. He totaled 144 yards in a decisive third quarter, including that magnificent 71-yard touchdown … that came after he lost his footing starting his route.

"The thing that stuck out today was he's making [plays] in all phases of the game," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said after Sunday's game . "On the extended plays, he's able to uncover and go become a target for our quarterback as well. So it's really in every stage of how we're playing offense. So it's pretty remarkable. He's a beast."

The most impressive fact about Smith-Njigba's dominance is that everyone on the other side of the ball knows it's coming … and they still can't stop it. Seattle doesn't have any other true receiving threats on the roster; Cooper Kupp, the Seahawks' second-leading receiver, is nearly a thousand yards behind JSN's current total of 1,207.

The Offensive Player of the Year award now tends to reward non-quarterback skill players; the last QB to win was Patrick Mahomes in 2018. It's also an award with a wide pool of candidates; the last repeat winner was Marshall Faulk, who won the award three straight times from 1999 to 2001.

Back to the question at the top: You're that offensive coordinator blessed with more talent than any team should have. So who would you choose to score that one-play touchdown, Jahmyr Gibbs or Jaxon Smith-Njigba?

Trick question. There's no wrong answer.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin’s Patriots warning takes a serious turn after Mike Vrabel’s controversial comments leave more questions than answers
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin has raised concerns about what could be happening inside the New England Patriots after their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich on
articles.body: Mike Tomlin has raised concerns about what could be happening inside the New England Patriots after their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich on Sunday, November 15. The former Pittsburgh Steelers coach was more troubled by Mike Vrabel’s postgame comments than the result itself, as the Patriots head coach spoke about players who complain instead of helping the team win. Tomlin now wonders if there is a bigger problem within New England.Mike Tomlin questions Mike Vrabel’s comments about Patriots players after Lions defeatThe Patriots had a difficult afternoon in Germany, losing 35-10 to the Lions while also dealing with injuries to quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown. However, it was Vrabel’s words after the game that caught Tomlin’s attention during NBC’s Football Night in America.Speaking about the importance of helping the team, Vrabel said, “Winners figure out ways to help the team win. They don’t b***h and complain, they try to find ways to help the team.”When reporters asked whether he was suggesting that his own players were complaining, Vrabel tried to explain what he meant. He said he was speaking about winners in general and wanted his team to have the right mindset.Tomlin, however, was not fully convinced by the explanation. He said the Patriots had faced several challenges this season, but the coach’s choice of words made him question whether something else was happening within the team.“What alarms me is what Coach just said there. I don’t know who he was speaking to, or what he was referring to, but certainly, there’s probably some fire along with that smoke,” Tomlin said.He added, “I wasn’t this concerned, to be quite honest with you, until I heard his postgame. And it makes me lean in and wonder what’s going on behind the scenes.”Tomlin’s concern was not a claim that there was a confirmed dispute between Vrabel and his players. Rather, he wanted to understand why the Patriots coach felt the need to make such a statement after the defeat.Drake Maye and A.J. Brown injuries add to Mike Vrabel’s problems as Patriots enter bye weekThe defeat was made worse by the loss of two important offensive players. Maye suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter after being sacked by Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. He left the field and did not return, forcing backup quarterback Tommy DeVito to take over.DeVito struggled to make an impact, completing 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception. With Maye’s injury still needing further tests, New England faces questions about who will lead its offense when the team returns from its bye week.A.J. Brown also failed to finish the game after suffering a hamstring injury in the second half. It was another setback for the wide receiver, who had already missed two games with ankle and knee problems before returning against Detroit. According to Boston.com, Vrabel said the team would check the severity of both injuries after returning home.There was another incident that brought attention to Vrabel after the defeat. The Patriots coach was seen spending time with fans at Augustiner Stammhaus, a German beer hall, just hours after the loss. Videos of him enjoying the evening spread online and drew criticism from some Patriots fans in the United States.New England now enters its bye week with a 5-5 record and sits second in the AFC East. The team is still in the playoff race, but its recent results and injury problems have made the remaining games more important. The Patriots have also lost three of their last four games, leaving Vrabel with several issues to address before their next matchup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Refs' Final Stats After Working Double Duty After FAA Stoppage Impacts Travel Schedules
articles.summary: The FAA's nationwide ground stop didn't impact the NFL's Week 10 schedule, but it caused plenty of turbulence for four NFL officials that were assigned two separate games on Sunday.
articles.body:
The FAA's nationwide ground stop didn't impact the NFL's Week 10 schedule, but it caused plenty of turbulence for four NFL officials that were assigned two separate games on Sunday.

The four officials called 30 penalties and reversed two out of three challenges on 242 plays in six hours and 15 minutes, ESPN's Kalyn Kahler reported. Perhaps most importantly, they avoided any major controversial calls.

According to Kahler, referee Don Willard, umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew began their day by officiating the Indianapolis Colts' 24-22 victory against the Miami Dolphins in Lucas Oil Stadium. After the game, a sprinter van drove them 110 miles southeast for their second assignment at Paycor Stadium, where the Cincinnati Bengals trounced the Pittsburgh Steelers in a 38-18 victory on Sunday Night Football.

"To best of our knowledge, no NFL official has worked two games in one day," the NFL Referees Association told NBC News . "Officials have worked two games in a week before, but we can't find an instance where one has worked a double header like this."

The NFL announced Saturday morning that it would reassign officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones . Eighteen officials worked at positions they had not worked this season, The Athletic's Mike Sando reported.

Only 7.1 flags were thrown per game in Week 10, the fewest this season in any week before Monday Night Football, according to Sando. That's particularly down from the start of the 2026 season, which had most accepted penalties through Week 4 since play-by-play data became available in 1978, per ESPN . Sando noted that teams averaged just 0.7 offensive holding calls, down from 1.8 over the past nine weeks.

Carl Cheffers was slated to serve as the referee in Indianapolis, and Clete Blakeman originally had the assignment in Cincinnati. Willard, a nine-year official, was named as the referee for both games. Blakeman had to drive eight hours for his reassignment in Green Bay, Kahler reported.

articles.title: Jordan Addison Set for Surgery, Latest on Vikings WR's Timeline to Return from Injury
articles.summary: After missing Sunday's 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison will be sidelined for multiple more weeks.
articles.body:
After missing Sunday's 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison will be sidelined for multiple more weeks.

Coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that Addison needs thumb surgery. His recovery period will be long enough to where an injured reserve designation is possible.

Addison hurt his thumb during last Friday's practice.

"He wanted to try to go (Sunday), just couldn't get there," O'Connell told reporters . "I don't anticipate it being a long-term kind of thing, something similar to what Donovan Jackson went through [last season] and how quickly he returned from that (Jackson missed three games after wrist surgery), but obviously being a receiver and catching the football, a little bit different there."

Addison's absence against the Packers allowed Myles Price to make a big impact. Price caught four passes for 49 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter.

The Vikings have eight games remaining in the regular season, so placing Addison on IR would keep him out for at least half of that stretch.

For the 2023 first-round pick, the injury compounds what has been a frustrating year. He has just one touchdown reception through seven games, and his 39.6 yards per contest are on pace to be a career low.

Addison seemingly stood to benefit from the arrival of quarterback Kirk Cousins. Instead, he'll have to wait to experience Cousins' effect on the passing game firsthand.

articles.title: Jets' Aaron Glenn Addresses Relinquishing Defensive Playcalling amid Hot-Seat Buzz
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing speculation surrounding his job security, New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn made a major adjustment that many didn't see coming.
articles.body:
Amid the ongoing speculation surrounding his job security, New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn made a major adjustment that many didn't see coming.

Glenn told reporters on Monday that he ceded defensive playcalling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. The second-year head coach had infamously said that playcalling was "my superpower" over the offseason.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

The change didn't do much for the Jets, who are still searching for answers after suffering their fifth straight loss and falling to 2-8. New York has allowed 31.6 points per game during the losing streak.

Duker is a first-time coordinator with no prior playcalling experience, but the players appear to still have some confidence in him.

"They have a very similar mindset in calling the defense," safety Dane Belton said of Glenn and Duker. "There wasn't much difference from my perspective."

The Jets will keep trying to find a solution to their defensive woes when they return to action in Week 11 against the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Injury, Timeline Updated by Packers' HC as Star Still Has 'Hurdles to Clear'
articles.summary: Micah Parsons is on track to return to the field for the Green Bay Packers before Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
Micah Parsons is on track to return to the field for the Green Bay Packers before Thanksgiving.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team plans on having the star pass-rusher available for its Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, even though he still has a "couple more hurdles to clear," per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

LaFleur also said Green Bay will "see where he is by the end of the week."

Parsons hasn't played this season as he recovers from a torn ACL he suffered in December.

He missed the rest of the 2025 campaign for Green Bay, including its postseason loss to the rival Chicago Bears. However, he might finally be on the field again for the NFC North club, which opened his practice window earlier this month.

Green Bay is on a bye for Week 11, so he has a bit more time to get ready for a Wednesday game.

This is also a critical time for the Packers in the postseason chase, as Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings dropped them to 6-4 and in last place in the competitive NFC North. Every other team in the division has just two losses, so the focus may eventually have to shift to the wild-card race.

And that game against the Rams is a critical one.

Green Bay, Los Angeles and the Seattle Seahawks are all 6-4 and tied in the race for the seventh and final seed in the NFC playoff picture. The Packers have the spot as of Monday because of conference record, but a head-to-head result against the Rams will go a long way toward determining wild-card positioning.

Parsons' return will give the Packers a much-needed boost, as he is one of the best defensive players in the league with a resume that includes three First-Team All-Pro selections, five Pro Bowl nods and five seasons with double-digit sacks.

It seems like that return is on track for the next time the team takes the field.

San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones was vibing as the team took the field on Sunday to some NBA YoungBoy in a video that has since gone viral.

articles.title: Cowboys Defense Called Out by Stephen Jones After Being on Wrong Side of History vs. 49ers
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones isn't happy about the state of the defense after the team gave 584 yards of offense to the San Francisco 49ers—the most ever allowed by the franchise at home—during Sunday's 46-40 loss.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones isn't happy about the state of the defense after the team gave 584 yards of offense to the San Francisco 49ers—the most ever allowed by the franchise at home—during Sunday's 46-40 loss.

Jones isn't ready to fully side with fans calling for the firings of head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, however.

"I certainly understand their frustration because there's no doubt that we're frustrated," he said during a Monday appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t Jon Machota of The Athletic). "We feel like the way we're playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better."

There's no understating just how bad the Dallas defense was against the Niners.

The Cowboys gave up three touchdowns of 66 or more yards on Sunday, 214 yards on the ground and allowed San Francisco to convert over half of their third-down attempts (6-of-11). The 49ers scored on seven of their 11 possessions and didn't turn the ball over.

And it spoiled a game that saw Dak Prescott throw for 343 yards, five touchdowns and a pick.

"I think offensively we do a good job," Jones said Monday. "In general, I'd say we move the ball well. As a whole, if you look at the, if you want to refer to it as the Schottenheimer Era, I'd say, yeah, our offense has been an offense that's played at a high level. (They've) been in the top half, top-third of the league, however you want to define it. But defensively, obviously we haven't. The last two years with Coach Schottenheimer as our head coach, our defense has been, unfortunately, predominantly in the back-third of the league, back-quarter of the league, however you want to define it. We haven't done a good job on the defensive side of the ball. We've struggled with that."

Schottenheimer called out the defense after the contest as well:

And he didn't exactly commit to Parker going forward:

For the Cowboys (4-6), it was a blown opportunity to move closer to the New York Giants (5-3-1) in the NFC East standings after the division leaders lost to the Washington Commanders (3-5-1) on Thursday. The division is as open as its been in years, but Dallas hasn't taken advantage, failing to string wins together.

"At the end of the day we're not doing what it takes to win these football games," Jones noted. "At times you feel like things are going in a good direction and then you have a second half, especially on the defensive side of the ball where you feel like you're taking one step forward and three steps back. This is obviously very frustrating. As this season goes, we're making things very difficult for ourselves to stay in the hunt."

articles.title: Vikings' Myles Price Denied Lambeau Leap by Packers Fans, Rookie Reacts in Funny Sideline Video
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers fans celebrating with the home team's players who do the Lambeau Leap after a touchdown is one of the most famous traditions in the NFL, but they weren't about to celebrate with a rival member of the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers fans celebrating with the home team's players who do the Lambeau Leap after a touchdown is one of the most famous traditions in the NFL, but they weren't about to celebrate with a rival member of the Minnesota Vikings.

Vikings wide receiver Myles Price scored a touchdown during Minnesota's 30-10 win on Sunday and attempted his own Lambeau Leap just to be pushed back by the fans.

"They wouldn't let me up," he said. "Everybody was pushing me back."

Price ultimately got the last laugh by helping lead his team to a key victory and pushing the Packers further back into last place in the NFC North.

articles.title: Ranking Patriots QB Options to Replace Injured Drake Maye
articles.summary: The New England Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye on the first drive of their previous game in Munich, Germany, and potentially for the rest of the 2026 season. At 5-5, they still have a shot at the playoffs with a capable fill-in starter.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye on the first drive of their previous game in Munich, Germany, and potentially for the rest of the 2026 season. At 5-5, they still have a shot at the playoffs with a capable fill-in starter.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Patriots are concerned that Maye fractured his ankle, and he's out indefinitely.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz added that New England will "explore the QB market" while on its Week 11 bye.

While the Patriots mull over the quarterback market, we'll rank their potential options among their backups, free agents, and players they could sign off practice squads.

These potential fill-in starters have played under Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, have a solid history as a backup signal-caller, or offer upside under an experienced play-caller.

Nick Mullens is a career backup, though he's started in at least three games in three of his nine NFL seasons, with the San Francisco 49ers (2018 and 2020) and the Minnesota Vikings (2023). He didn't lead either team to the playoffs, but that doesn't mean the experienced signal-caller is incapable of doing so.

Mullens has thrown for 6,448 yards, 34 touchdowns and 31 interceptions with a 66 percent completion rate. If McDaniels can help him limit turnovers, he can be a decent starter in relief.

In his pro career, Mullens has played under respected play-callers, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, Vikings lead skipper Kevin O'Connell and currently Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen.

Although Mullens wouldn't be a headline signing off the Jaguars' practice squad, he could be an alternative option if the Patriots favor experience.

In 2023 and 2025, Jake Browning took over for an injured Joe Burrow. In the first of those two years, he threw for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions with a league-leading 70.4 percent completion rate. The Cincinnati Bengals went 4-3 with him as their starter that year.

Last season, Browning didn't look as sharp filling in for Burrow, throwing for 771 yards, six touchdowns and eight interceptions with a 64.8 percent completion rate. After he made three starts, the Bengals replaced him with Joe Flacco, whom they acquired from the Cleveland Browns.

Still, Browning would bring quality experience, replacing a high-end starter for a team with playoff aspirations. He would be familiar with the pressure in that situation, with 10 career starts in Cincinnati.

New England could sign Browning off the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad.

If the New England Patriots are open to adding a high-upside quarterback, Will Levis may be a top option on their target list.

The Tennessee Titans moved up to select Levis with the first pick in the second round of the 2023 draft. In his first two seasons with the Titans, he threw for 3,899 yards, 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions with a 61 percent completion rate, but his turnover-prone play and inability to stay healthy cost him the starting job.

Levis is 27, and with only two years of starting experience, he can still develop into a decent starter.

The Patriots can look to Malik Willis and his development with the Green Bay Packers and Miami Dolphins over the last few years as an example of a player who capitalized on new opportunities after a rocky start to his career in Tennessee.

Levi's arm strength and mobility are appealing physical tools that could earn him a shot in New England. The Patriots can sign him off the New York Jets' practice squad.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that even though the Patriots will explore quarterback options, backup Tommy DeVito is expected to start in place of Drake Maye, which makes the most sense because he's learned offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels' system over the last two seasons.

In August of 2025, New England claimed DeVito off waivers. He didn't play in any regular-season games until last Sunday in Munich, Germany. The fourth-year pro had a rough outing against the Detroit Lions, throwing for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

However, DeVito should be more prepared following a bye week and a full week of practice with the first-team offense.

In 2023, DeVito was a serviceable fill-in starter for the New York Giants in place of Daniel Jones, throwing for 1,101 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions with a 64 percent completion rate.

In all likelihood, DeVito will get the first shot at starting at center in Maye's absence.

The Patriots could reunite McDaniels with Jimmy Garoppolo. They started their pro careers in New England and worked together through the 2023 season with the Las Vegas Raiders.

In 2016, Garoppolo showed promise in two starts with the Patriots, throwing for 502 yards and four touchdowns under McDaniels. New England won both games. Yet the club traded him to the San Francisco 49ers the following year, essentially choosing 40-year-old Tom Brady over his potential successor.

Garoppolo went on to have a solid career with the 49ers, throwing for 13,599 yards, 82 touchdowns and 42 interceptions with a 67.6 percent completion rate in six seasons. He also helped lead San Francisco to a Super Bowl appearance but struggled in the playoffs , throwing for four touchdowns and six interceptions with a 60.6 percent completion rate.

After the Raiders released Derek Carr in the 2023 offseason, they signed Garoppolo. At that time, McDaniels was Las Vegas' head coach, so the move made sense. Yet Garoppolo flopped as a starter with the Silver and Black, throwing for 1,205 yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions in seven games before the team benched him for Aidan O'Connell.

Nonetheless, if the Patriots want a stopgap quarterback with a wealth of big-game experience, Garoppolo fits the bill, and his familiarity with McDaniels could appeal to the coaching staff. The 35-year-old is an available free agent.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Cass report author says she does not support draft conversion practices bill
articles.summary: The gender care review author says the bill’s wording risks "serious unintended consequences" for parents and therapists.
articles.body:
The author of the independent review into gender identity services for young people says she doesn't support the current draft bill banning conversion practices - having previously welcomed it.

Baroness Cass said the current wording of the bill risked "serious unintended consequences" for parents of children suffering gender distress, or medical professionals working in that area.

She was speaking at a parliamentary committee scrutinising the bill, which the government said would protect LGBT people in England and Wales.

A government spokesperson said they welcomed her comments and would take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as they "want to get this ban right".

Conversion practices are generally described as interventions, treatments or activities designed to change or suppress someone's sexual orientation or gender identity.

This can sometimes happen in religious or family settings and can be very distressing for the person at the centre of it.

There have been long-running campaigns in the UK to outlaw such practices, and in its 2024 manifesto, the Labour party promised to introduce a bill banning them.

When the government introduced its draft legislation in June this year, Baroness Cass was quoted in the publicity for it .

In it, she said: "I am pleased to see that the government is bringing forward legislation which not only gives a clearer definition of what conversion practices are, compared to previous drafts, but also what they are not".

She went on to say she looked forward to the bill receiving further scrutiny before it became law.

But asked at the Draft Conversion Practices Bill committee if she supported the bill's current form, she said simply "no".

Baroness Cass said the increased "polarisation" used in the debate around gender meant people may use the new law in a way that wasn't intended.

The current wording of the bill requires the victim to suffer "serious harm to the individual's physical or mental health, or serious alarm or distress to the individual which has a substantial adverse effect on their usual day-to-day activities."

But Baroness Cass said she worried this wording left open the possibility of "vexatious" complaints that could put therapists working with young gender-distressed people at risk of prosecution.

"If a young person, for example, has been sexually abused, any discussion about it is going to be incredibly triggering.

"But if you can't therapeutically work through it without any reference to it, and that's the problem," she said.

She said that professionals working at the new NHS Gender Dysphoria Clinics were concerned that even complaints processes that didn't result in a prosecution could be damaging.

Baroness Cass also raised concerns about the possible impact the new law could have on families.

She said that, for instance, if a parent stopped a child's money if they thought they might buy a "breast binder or hormones" that this may also fall within the scope of the bill and result in prosecution.

Asked about her apparent support for the bill when it was first published, Baroness Cass said that she was in favour of the idea but hadn't had the time to read the details before the press release was to be published, but went ahead and gave the quote anyway.

When she published her report on gender identity services for young people in 2024, she described conversion practices as "abhorrent". She says she still feels no LGBT people should be subjected to conversion practices.

She told the committee she wants "a bill that protects the people it's supposed to protect, but doesn't accidentally entrap those who you don't want to [entrap]."

The government said: "We want to get this ban right, which is why we have put this draft bill forward for pre-legislative scrutiny.

"We welcome both Baroness Cass's support for taking action to end abusive conversion practices, and her comments on the need for legislation to avoid adverse consequences.

"We will take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as we move forward in ending almost a decade of delay for LGBT+ people who should never have to suffer abuse in an effort to change who they are."

articles.title: NFL promoting that Raiders coaches and players spoke to Francisco Mendoza in Spanish is a virtue signal stunt
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders' Spanish-language communication with quarterback Fernando Mendoza felt forced, scripted and not organic.
articles.body: I considered writing this column in Spanish because I've covered the NFL for 36 years and, apparently, now that Fernando Mendoza is a starting quarterback, America's most popular professional sports league wants everyone to know it embraces Spanish. What a time to be alive! I was born in Cuba and embrace Spanish, too. It's my first language. But I've been doing my job in English seemingly forever because I live in the United States and English is the language here. And an NFL locker room has had about as much to do with communicating in Spanish as it does in Swahili. But since Mendoza is of Cuban descent (yeah, we're everywhere) and his parents are of Cuban descent, and his grandparents came from Cuba, someone at the NFL decided this an opportunity for some sort of outreach to Hispanics. So when the Las Vegas Raiders had players and coaches speak some Spanish to Mendoza on Sunday during their game, the NFL saw this as a chance to pump itself as a global brand. Did I mention Mendoza happened to be mic'd up to pick up teammate Aidan O'Connell tell him to "respira," which means breathe in Spanish? What a coincidence. FERNANDO MENDOZA EMBRACES 'ONCE-IN-A-LIFETIME' CHANCE AS RAIDERS' QB1, CREDITS KIRK COUSINS' MENTORSHIP The mic caught one Las Vegas coach throwing a random Spanish word here and there at Mendoza on the sideline. And the league took those moments and did a look-at-us post on X to show that it's got some Spanish going on. There is a phrase for this in my country: Virtue signaling. THREE NFL TEAMS ROASTED FOR CELEBRATING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' DAY ON COLUMBUS DAY, WHICH NO TEAM EVEN MENTIONED It's not only unwelcome but opens up the NFL for mockery because it is not organic. It feels forced. Why? Firstly, Mendoza is American. Yes, his cultural origins cannot be denied. But he was born in this country and understandably speaks English much more fluently than he does Spanish – like many Hispanics his age living in the United States. Secondly, is the NFL doing this for its quarterbacks of German descent? Or Italian? Or any other ethnicity? Thirdly, the folks trying to somehow talk to Mendoza on the sideline in his non-native tongue weren't really speaking Spanish. They weren't stringing cogent sentences together. They were merely throwing out a Spanish word here and there. It seemed forced. At one point, a Raiders assistant coach told Mendoza, "Tu eres chingon." The phrase is used by Mexicans and translates to 'You are awesome." I think that's true because, although I speak Spanish fluently, I had to go look it up because I am not Mexican. And neither is Mendoza. And Spanish spoken in some countries, such as Mexico, is different from Spanish spoken in other countries, such as Cuba. Breaking! People of Puerto Rican, Honduran, Mexican, Dominican or Venezuelan descent playing or coaching in the NFL don't all speak the same kind of Spanish. Some, like Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, aren't comfortable speaking Spanish at all. So those players and coaches might look at someone telling them "Tu eres chingon" just like someone from Iowa or West Virginia might. People in Texas speak differently than those in New York. Americans go to England and understand that our shared language is not identical. So it is with Spanish. That's why this gimmick post by the NFL actually shows how little the league actually understands Hispanics. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Look, it may seem nice that the NFL tried to give Mendoza's ancestry a tip of the cap. But anyone doing their homework would know that the first Raiders quarterback with Hispanic roots was Tom Flores, who also happened to coach the team to two Super Bowl victories. He never had any of his coaches or players speak to Jim Plunkett in Spanish even though, you know, Plunkett was also of Hispanic descent. Then again, virtue signaling wasn't a thing in the NFL back then. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Status as Colts QB1 Explained by HC Amid 3-7 Record, Benching Buzz
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters that Daniel Jones will remain the starting quarterback despite his disastrous performance in Sunday's 24-22 victory over the Miami Dolphins, per ESPN's Stephen Holder.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters that Daniel Jones will remain the starting quarterback despite his disastrous performance in Sunday's 24-22 victory over the Miami Dolphins, per ESPN's Stephen Holder .

The 2026 season has not gone how Indianapolis had hoped. Since starting last season with an 8-1 record, the Colts have lost 14 of their last 17 regular-season games.

While there's plenty of blame to go around, Jones deserves his fair share. The eight-year veteran has completed less than 60 percent of his passes for 1,830 yards with seven touchdowns and a league-high 12 interceptions.

Steichen was asked what Jones does on game days to remain the starter, according to The Athletic's James Boyd .

"There's a lot of things that play into it," Steichen said. "Obviously, we know, he knows he's gotta take care of the ball better, first and foremost. It's not all about one guy, I think it takes all 11 to do their job at a high level. … But he does lead our team each and every week to get ready for those games on Sunday."

The Colts narrowly escaped defeat against the one-win Dolphins as Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Indianapolis ended seven of its 12 drives without picking up a single first down.

When asked if team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has any input on the team's starter, Steichen said he "has those conversations with her, but she lets me go," per Boyd .

Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract extension with the offseason, per Spotrac .

"I'm not going to get into contract stuff," Steichen said when asked if the Jones' contract had anything to do with his continued role as the starter.

articles.title: Boston Globe compares Dianna Russini to Bob Woodward amid Vrabel-sourcing scandal
articles.summary: The Boston Globe compares NFL reporter Dianna Russini to Bob Woodward over her closeness to Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, but the paper sees a difference.
articles.body: The Boston Globe argues that NFL reporter Dianna Russini might be best described as the modern-day Bob Woodward. Last week, Russini returned to media after a seven-month hiatus following various outlets obtaining photos of her in a pool, at a bar, at a casino, and renting a private boat (while pregnant) with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Russini resigned from The Athletic in April amid an internal investigation into her failure to disclose her relationship with a source and subject, whether romantic or not. She now hosts a weekly podcast for offshore gambling company BetUS. DIANNA RUSSINI'S CRINGE PODCAST DEBUT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT THE VIABILITY OF HER COMEBACK Despite the unusual circumstances, the Globe's Joan Vennochi drew parallels between Russini and Woodward, who also got too close to a source. "There’s no compromising photo of Woodward in a hot tub with Richard Darman, the powerful official in two long-ago presidential administrations, as there was of Russini and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel while she was reporting on the NFL," Vennochi wrote. "But in a piece in The New Yorker titled 'The Danger of Getting Too Close to a Source,' which is drawn from his new book, 'Secrets: A Reporter’s Memoir,' Woodward describes an intimate relationship with Darman that, figuratively speaking, put him in similar hot water. In the article referenced, Woodward acknowledges that he "should have realized the danger" of his relationship with Darman but also that "the information flow and the time with Darman was so valuable." The Globe article did, however, distinguish the two reporters in one way: "[O]nce sex is involved, or speculated about, as it was with Russini and Vrabel (although neither has acknowledged it), such a relationship is automatically wrong for the journalist. "But take the sex out of it — which no one ever can — and, as all journalists know, the same ethics questions arise. At what point does closeness not only cloud objectivity but also hamper the ability to tell the full truth if that truth hurts your source?," wrote Vennochi. BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL Despite the bizarre comparison, the Globe misses the point: Woodward acknowledged the error in his judgment. Russini hasn't. Russini looks worse today than she did when the first photo of her and Vrabel alone at an adults-only resort in Arizona leaked. She has taken no accountability. Instead, she has blamed the media and unnamed "lies" for her circumstances. Last week, ahead of her return, Russini cast herself as a heroine for other women. "I really hope that I can be someone other women see: you can pick yourself up, get back in there and not be afraid," Russini told People. At the very least, Russini should do what Woodward and countless other journalists have done: admit she crossed boundaries with a source and vow to do better. Instead, she maintains her innocence as if the rest of us are that gullible. Her arrogance continues to be her downfall. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If anything, Russini has positioned herself as the poster child for how not to handle getting too close to a source. She is hardly the sympathetic figure she depicts herself as. The comparison to Woodward only makes her refusal to take accountability look worse.

articles.title: Broncos' Payton Responds to Chargers' Harbaugh Calling Out 'Loophole' in Failed Henley Trade
articles.summary: On Thursday, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh accused the Denver Broncos of exercising a "loophole" after backing out of a trade for linebacker Daiyan Henley due to a failed physical.
articles.body:
On Thursday, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh accused the Denver Broncos of exercising a "loophole" after backing out of a trade for linebacker Daiyan Henley due to a failed physical.

Denver head coach Sean Payton responded on Monday.

"I saw it all. There's no loophole," he told reporters . "It just is part of the trade process, every step of the way."

The Broncos originally agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to Los Angeles before Tuesday's deadline but backed out after Henley's physical.

Harbaugh, however, suggested that the Broncos tried to use the results of the medical exam as a bargaining chip.

"The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation and we wouldn't, and we didn't," he told reporters on Thursday. "In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."

"It's a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that," he continued. "It's a medical grade, it's a pass/fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren't gonna pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and fill in the blank. I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."

While Payton didn't agree with Harbaugh's assessment of the situation, he didn't offer further details.

"I'm not going to get into specifics," he said. "[Henley's] a prospect we thought—and still do—very highly of. It just didn't work out. It's not uncommon with trades. That's kind of where it went. I'll leave it at that."

Henley, 26, has registered 51 tackles, two fumble recoveries, one forced fumble, one interception and half a sack this season.

articles.body: Tyreek Hill is taking an unusual route in his fight to return to professional football. With his NFL future still hanging in the balance, the former Miami Dolphins star has turned to a physician whose work with Olympic champion Usain Bolt has earned him global recognition. The move has added fresh intrigue to Hill’s recovery, especially as speculation about a possible Kansas City Chiefs reunion continues to grow. However, one major obstacle remains. Before any franchise can bring him back, Hill must prove that his injured knee is ready for the demands of the NFL.Tyreek Hill turns to Usain Bolt’s doctor for knee recoveryHill recently travelled to Munich, Germany, to seek treatment from Dr. Hans-Wilhelm Müller-Wohlfahrt, a renowned sports physician known for working with elite athletes. Müller-Wohlfahrt spent more than 40 years working with Bayern Munich and served the German national football team between 1995 and 2018. articles.title: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson reportedly confirmed to have torn ACL, ending his 2026 season
articles.summary: Hutchinson sustained the injury during Detroit's win over the Patriots in Munich, celebrating a sack early in the game.
articles.body:
Fears that Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee were confirmed after additional exams, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . Though tests reportedly revealed no other significant damage to Hutchinson's knee, he is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season with the injury.

Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series versus the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich. After sacking New England's Drake Maye, Detroit's fifth-year star jumped in celebration and landed awkwardly on his right leg. Hutchinson immediately went to the turf. As teammates and players approached, he gestured to the front of his right knee.

Hutchinson reportedly underwent an MRI after Detroit's 35-10 win that showed a torn ACL. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the defensive end would undergo further testing when the team returned to the U.S. before making an official announcement.

"We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell said postgame, via the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi . "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy."

Meanwhile, a fan captured video of Hutchinson in a wheelchair at the airport prior to the Lions traveling back to Michigan on Sunday.

Maye sustained an injury to his ankle on the same play and the Patriots fear the QB may have suffered a fracture that would end his season . The third-year star stayed in Germany for additional testing that could determine if he needs surgery, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed during a radio interview Monday.

In nine games this season, Hutchinson recorded 6 sacks and 24 total tackles in addition to 1 pass defended and 1 forced fumble.

Hutchinson's torn ACL is the second serious, season-ending injury that he has sustained during his NFL career. During the 2024 season, he suffered a broken fibula and tibia in his left leg during a Week 6 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Hutchinson recovered to play in all 17 games last year, compiling 14.5 sacks.

The Lions' 2022 first-round draft pick (No. 2 overall) out of Michigan, Hutchinson has been named to two Pro Bowls and earned second-team All-Pro honors during his career. He's compiled 49 sacks in 65 games with 200 tackles and 5 interceptions.

Last year, Hutchinson signed a four-year, $180 million contract extension (including $141 million in guaranteed money). That extension kicks in next season following the fifth-year option the Lions picked up this year.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald says 'Sam's our quarterback' amid chatter that Drew Lock should start for Seahawks over Darnold
articles.summary: The Seahawks are now 4-0 this season with Lock, who's played objectively better than Sam Darnold in place of the injured Seattle starter in four appearances.
articles.body:
Drew Lock threw for 240 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday as the Seattle Seahawks secured a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .

The Seahawks are now 4-0 this season with Lock, who's played objectively better than Sam Darnold in place of the injured Seattle starter in four appearances. This has prompted chatter amongst fans that maybe the Seahawks are better off with Lock as their full-time starting quarterback.

That chatter reached head coach Mike Macdonald on Monday. He was quick to shoot down the idea during an interview with Seattle Sports radio .

"Drew's been fantastic. He's been phenomenal," Macdonald said. "But Sam's our quarterback. … To have Drew as our backup and play the way he has has been awesome."

It's an interesting spot for the Seahawks. Darnold had the second-best season of his career in his first season with Seattle last year, and the Seahawks won a Super Bowl.

Seattle's defense and playmakers on offense in Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III were the primary driving forces of that championship run. But Darnold played his role well on a championship team. And moving away from a Super Bowl-winning quarterback the very next season could certainly be seen as a drastic step.

But outside of last season and his 2024 campaign with the Minnesota Vikings, Darnold's body of work leaves a lot to be desired. A former No. 3 draft pick, Darnold was firmly in bust territory after bouncing around and failing to hold jobs with the Jets, Panthers and 49ers before landing in Minnesota.

That version of Darnold is the one who's showed up in 2026.

In seven starts this season, including the season-opener in which he played just one possession due to injury, Darnold's completed 60.2% of his passes for 7 yards per attempt with 10 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. Those are generally not numbers fitting of an NFL starter. The Seahawks are 2-4 in Darnold's starts excluding the season-opener, and his turnovers are a significant reason why.

By comparison, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 9 yards per attempt with 7 touchdowns and no interceptions. It's a small sample size from a career backup against a softer slate (Patriots, Cardinals, Cardinals, Raiders) than Darnold's faced (Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, Bears). With two lost fumbles against the Raiders, Lock is not turnover free. But the numbers in his favor are compelling.

Macdonald, meanwhile, had to stop himself short with his praise of Darnold Monday before shifting to attribute Darnold's struggles to injury.

"We saw what Sam's been capable of both last year and in the — the beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said. … "Sam's our starting quarterback. I can't wait for him to be fully healthy probably for the first time."

The Seahawks have a bye this week. They'll come out of the bye for a key division showdown against the NFC-best 8-1 San Francisco 49ers on the other side.

Macdonald told reporters Monday that the Seahawks are "optimistic" that Darnold will be ready to return from a quadriceps injury to face the 49ers.

If he's healthy, expect Darnold to play. If he struggles in a Seahawks loss, expect this conversation to be renewed.

articles.title: Matt Cassel Jokes About Signing With Mike Vrabel, Patriots Amid Garoppolo Rumors After Maye Injury
articles.summary: A familiar name for New England Patriots fans is throwing his hat in the ring to become the new quarterback, although it came in a joking manner.
articles.body:
A familiar name for New England Patriots fans is throwing his hat in the ring to become the new quarterback, although it came in a joking manner.

Matt Cassel, who last played in the NFL during the 2018 campaign and is 44 years old, took to social media and encouraged Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to reach out about the opening after Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury during Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions.

Cassel was responding to a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz that said New England was potentially interested in adding another of its former quarterbacks in Jimmy Garoppolo even though Tommy DeVito is expected to be the starter.

DeVito entered Sunday's game following Maye's setback but struggled while going 12-of-24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the 35-10 defeat.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported there is concern Maye could miss the entire season due to a fractured ankle, but the quarterback is remaining in Germany to undergo additional tests.

Cassel played for the Patriots during the first four seasons of his career from 2005-08 before stops with the Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans and Lions.

He famously filled in for an injured Tom Brady in 2008 and went 10-5 as a starter. He was also a Pro Bowler in 2010 for the Chiefs but was primarily a backup for the latter portion of his career.

Ironically, Vrabel was Cassel's teammate with the Patriots, including during that 2008 campaign. That means he probably knows how to reach the former quarterback, but it would be quite the surprise if he took the 44-year-old's offer seriously.

articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers secured their eighth win of the season on Sunday after defeating the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 in an offensive shootout.

However, if there's one coach you want in an offensively driven game, it's 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. Few coaches match his ability as a play caller, which he has demonstrated throughout his 10 seasons in San Francisco. The 49ers hired Shanahan in 2017 after he held multiple offensive coordinator roles.

On Monday, following Sunday's win, the team announced that Shanahan had officially reached 90 regular-season wins. That makes him just the third coach in franchise history to reach the milestone.

He joins George Seifert, who recorded 98 wins, and Bill Walsh, who finished with 92. Shanahan is now closing in on Walsh's mark and could surpass him this season. He's also chasing Seifert's record to become the winningest head coach in 49ers regular-season history.

Someone else added, "If we can figure out how to stay healthy, we can win it all this year."

Another person wrote, "Add in 9 playoff wins and he is sitting at 99 total (reg & post season) wins. Let's get to 100 on Sunday night."

"If not for the losses during 2017 season rebuild year and 2018 jimmy G injury lost season, it would be higher. Same with 2020,2024 and almost 2025."

Through more than 150 regular-season games in his 10 seasons in San Francisco, Shanahan now holds a 90-68 record, giving him a .567 winning percentage.

He's also found success in the playoffs, going 9-5 and leading the team to two Super Bowl appearances, although the 49ers fell short in both.

Shanahan's won three division titles and could capture his fourth NFC West title this season if the standings hold. The 49ers currently hold a three-game cushion over the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, who are both 6-4.

articles.title: Jaguars’ Parker Washington Reminds Everyone How Dynamic He Is
articles.summary: After a couple of quiet games, Parker Washington reminded everyone how special he is.
articles.body:
When the Jacksonville Jaguars began their 2025 season, wide receiver Parker Washington was an afterthought.

Entering his third season, Washington hadn't been a major part of the offense in his first two years and wasn't expected to be in 2025.

After all, Jacksonville already had Brian Thomas Jr., who looked like he was well on his way to becoming one of the NFL's best WRs after his Pro Bowl rookie campaign in 2024. The Jaguars had also made a huge trade in the 2025 NFL Draft, moving up to select two-way star Travis Hunter with the second overall pick.

With BTJ and Hunter entrenched as the team's top WR duo, Washington was expected to continue his role as a dangerous punt returner who could contribute a bit on offense.

That's not how things turned out. Thomas regressed in a huge way all season, and Hunter, who didn't make the immediate impact most expected, was lost for the season after only seven games.

The Jaguars traded for Jakobi Meyers before the trade deadline. Meyers and Washington became Jacksonville's top WR duo as the team finished the regular season on an eight-game winning streak en route to a 13-4 record.

Washington went from afterthought to the Jaguars' leading receiver, blowing away his career highs in most statistical categories.

He was expected to sign a lucrative extension in the offseason. However, that never materialized , and his price has only gone up since.

Washington had a phenomenal offseason and started the year on fire, removing any doubt that he had truly developed into an elite receiver.

Over the past month, Washington cooled off a bit. Against the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens, Washington only caught three total passes despite the team piling up 75 points over the two games.

However, Washington reminded everyone how dynamic he is in Jacksonville's 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans.

Against the Titans, Washington set a new career high with 152 receiving yards on seven catches. His touchdown grab capped off the Jaguars' flawless opening drive and set the tone for the entire game.

Washington continued making big plays throughout, including a beautiful toe-drag catch along the sidelines, showing off his immaculate body control and awareness.

If anyone thought Washington's previous two games were a sign of things to come, he quickly put those thoughts to rest with his stellar performance.

The fact remains that Washington is the clear alpha of one of the league's most potent passing offenses and one of the most dynamic, explosive wide receivers in the NFL.

Washington's meteoric rise from afterthought to bona fide star has transformed the Jaguars into one of the NFL's best teams.

With Washington leading a terrific group of offensive weapons, Jacksonville is now one of the favorites to reach the Super Bowl for the first time in franchise history.

articles.title: "Reaching Out to Me in DMs": NFL Insider Shares Chiefs Rookie Emmett Johnson's Struggles Before Finding Fame With Patrick Mahomes & Co.
articles.summary: Emmett Johnson once had to message a reporter just to get college programs to notice him. On Sunday, he spent the afternoon running through an NFL defense in...
articles.body:
Emmett Johnson once had to message a reporter just to get college programs to notice him. On Sunday, he spent the afternoon running through an NFL defense in his first career start.

The Chiefs rookie carried 22 times for 101 yards and caught six passes for 70 more. He scored two touchdowns in a 35-13 win over the Falcons, and the 171 yards from scrimmage included his first 100-yard rushing game as a pro. NFL Insider Jordan Schultz shared a video explaining why this means more than a box score.

"Get this: his parents immigrated from civil war-torn Liberia. He ends up becoming Mr. Football in the state of Minnesota, and even then he only has one major college scholarship offer from Nebraska. And I remember Emmett reaching out to me on DMs. We were texting, 'Hey, can you help me get my name out there?' because colleges simply were not calling," Schultz said.

Nebraska's athletic site says Johnson's parents came to the United States as teenagers after leaving Liberia during its civil war. They wanted a better future for their children, and they raised him in Minneapolis.

He starred at Richfield Holy Angels and still got the cold shoulder. His first offer came from Northern Iowa, and camps at Minnesota, Iowa and Iowa State ended without one.

Nebraska finally offered after an official visit to Lincoln, late in his senior year.

The Huskers got the better end of that deal. In 2025, Johnson ran for 1,451 yards and led the Big Ten, adding 12 rushing touchdowns and 46 catches.

The Chiefs noticed, and so did a certain coordinator. Schultz said Eric Bieniemy "really laid the groundwork" for Kansas City to target him.

"This is a guy I have to have in my running back room," Schultz said, describing Bieniemy's view.

There is a fun detail behind that. Former All-Pro Maurice Jones-Drew said on his podcast that Bieniemy called him for running back advice, and he pushed Johnson hard.

When the Chiefs turned in their card, Bieniemy texted him: "Hey, got your guy." Kansas City had traded up with the Steelers to take Johnson 161st overall in the fifth round.

Johnson even keeps a list on his phone of the 160 players picked ahead of him. That is petty in the best possible way.

Then came the twist. The Chiefs signed Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, to a three-year deal worth up to $45 million in March.

That could have buried a fifth-round rookie. Instead, Schultz said, the pairing gave Kansas City two backs who can catch the ball.

"The perfect type of running back for that offense, because he was so comfortable catching the ball out of the backfield, as well as his running style: physical, violent, and yet electric with the explosives," Schultz said.

Johnson showed that on November 1 against Denver. He caught five passes for 128 yards, including a 73-yard touchdown for his first in the NFL, in a 28-24 loss.

Mahomes liked what he saw. "We're going to need more of it," the quarterback said afterward.

Two weeks later, Walker missed the Atlanta game with a groin injury, and Johnson got his chance. He scored first on a 12-yard catch from Mahomes, who threw five touchdown passes.

Johnson stayed humble afterward. "Just trusting in God," he said.

Schultz isn't losing sight of the bigger picture either. He credited Johnson's skills as part of why Mahomes is "playing some of the best football he's played in years."

Colleges were not calling back then. Chiefs fans cannot stop dialing his number now.
