articles.title: Brissett Loses Ravens Debut to Chargers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Herbert, Henry, Top Players
articles.summary: Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers are finally in the win column.
articles.body:
Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers are finally in the win column.

Los Angeles defeated the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 in Monday's AFC matchup at M&T Bank Stadium. It seemed as if the Ravens might escape with a win in Jacoby Brissett's first start for his new team, but Zay Flowers lost a fumble while fighting for extra yardage in the final minutes.

Chargers Post Dillon Brooks Laughing at LeBron Meme to Troll NFL Analysts All Picking Ravens to Win

Baltimore had one last opportunity, but Brissett's Hail Mary fell to the ground.

The Ravens are now in dire straits in the AFC playoff picture at 4-6 following a fifth consecutive loss. Brissett couldn't stop the slide in his first game since coming over via trade from the Arizona Cardinals, and they are multiple games back of the postseason.

If there was ever a real opportunity for the Chargers to get their first win, it was Monday with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley sidelined with injuries. While Baltimore responded to the situation by trading for Brissett instead of continuing to rely on Joe Fagnano, the new signal-caller still isn't a two-time MVP like Jackson.

And that was clear in the first half as the Chargers forced punts on Baltimore's first three possessions and also picked off Brissett when Del'Shawn Phillips caught a deflected ball. That interception set up a touchdown drive for the visitors, which Omarion Hampton finished with a physical fourth-down conversion at the goal line.

While Los Angeles built a 17-10 halftime advantage behind that touchdown and the game's opening score on a 22-yard run from Herbert, it wasn't all bad news for the Ravens.

Derrick Henry found the end zone and moved into seventh place on the NFL's all-time touchdown list. That run, which finished a drive that included key completions to Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman, kept Baltimore within striking distance heading into the second half.

Still, the Chargers bottled him up in the early going and held him to minus-one rushing yards in a stunning first half for the future Hall of Famer.

The Ravens just remaining within striking distance was a theme for much of the second half, as the two teams traded field goals and missed opportunities. One of those missed chances came when Ja'Kobi Lane failed to haul in a pass by the goal line that could have set up another touchdown and given the home team some momentum.

To Baltimore's credit, it did find the end zone on its next drive as Brissett moved it down the field before Henry finished the drive with a touchdown. It was a similar script to its first-half touchdown and cut the deficit to just three points in the fourth quarter.

The momentum continued as the Ravens got the ball back with a chance to win, but Flowers fumble proved to be the biggest play.

Now they will look to bounce back with a road game against the Carolina Panthers, while the Chargers will attempt to win two in a row when they host the New York Jets.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 11: Can the Browns keep winning in dramatic fashion?
articles.summary: The Browns are on a roll in close games, and now their playoff hopes are realistic.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Cleveland Browns have been through this type of season before. It has just been a long time.

In 1979, the Browns had seven fourth-quarter drives to win games. In the 1980 season they were 11-5 and nine of the wins came by one score. That group got the nickname of the Kardiac Kids . Brian Sipe became a Cleveland legend, and won the 1980 NFL MVP award.

The 2026 Browns aren't at that level yet, but they're getting close. After rallying to beat the Houston Texans on a touchdown with 53 seconds left , the Browns are the first team in NFL history to win each of its first six games by four or fewer points, according to ESPN Insights . Every one of those wins has included a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. It has been a magical, improbable run.

"We're going to figure something out about starting a hell of a lot faster," Browns head coach Todd Monken said, according to the team's transcripts. "But our guys continue to fight, and they battle, and they don't, they don't blink. Which is probably more important than starting fast, is when you have guys that continue to fight."

Whether it's sustainable might be irrelevant. Suddenly, the 6-4 Browns are in great shape to make the playoffs.

With the New England Patriots likely in for a big drop after Drake Maye's ankle injury and the Browns knocking the Texans back while also clinching the head-to-head tiebreaker, Cleveland's playoff hopes got a lot brighter Sunday. There was another assist on Monday night, when the previously winless Chargers beat the Ravens, knocking Baltimore back to 4-6. The Browns would be the seventh seed if the season ended today and they're a game up on any other team in the running. It's hard to find a team behind them — Patriots, Ravens, Raiders, Texans — that's going to make a big push. Three of those teams' quarterbacks are either injured or traded and 3-6 Houston is miles behind now because of the tiebreaker.

In Week 1, the Browns were blown out 34-10 by the Jaguars and there were plenty of jokes about how they were already tanking for a quarterback . Now Cleveland is 6-4 heading into a well deserved bye week.

"Isn't that cool? Isn't that awesome?" Monken said. "I mean, holy s***. There's no other way to put it, man."

There are still seven games to go and like Monken said, the Browns have to figure out how to play better in the first three quarters of games to win enough to get a playoff berth. But they have already stacked six wins and are in the clear lead for a wild-card spot. Cleveland fans couldn't have expected a playoff berth, but a fun start to the season has the Browns well within range.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 10:

1. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2, Last week: 1)

One of the signs of a good team is the ability to blow out bad teams. The Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans was their fifth win this season by 17 or more points, and it came with Jacksonville gambling that it could give trade additions defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III the week off. In more than half of Jacksonville's games, it has throttled its opponent. The Jags' point differential of +125 is 37 points better than the Bills, who are second.

The Jaguars haven't played a tough schedule, but it actually gets easier. Their remaining games against teams with a winning record come against the Giants, Bears and Steelers. The Jaguars are going to put up a very good record and are just hoping the other top teams in the AFC, most notably Buffalo, lose some.

The 49ers cooked the Cowboys' defense , putting up 46 points and 584 yards. Dallas' defense is dreadful but it's still hard to pile up close to 600 yards in any NFL game.

The way the 49ers have climbed to the top of the NFL in yards per game is worth studying. Brock Purdy was famously Mr. Irrelevant in the draft and now he's an MVP candidate. Christian McCaffrey was at a point in which age and touches should have started to chip away at his effectiveness, but he is tied for the NFL lead with 13 total touchdowns. Draft experts laughed at the Kaelon Black pick in the third round; he's one of the best backup running backs in the league. Deebo Samuel Sr.'s career looked like it might be over after last season, but he has five touchdowns in six games. The 49ers had to give up only a sixth-round draft pick for Keenan Allen in a trade and he had five catches for 61 yards on Sunday.

The conclusion: Kyle Shanahan is your NFL Coach of the Year.

Beating the Jets doesn't seem to be that impressive, but it was to Bills head coach Joe Brady. His explanation made sense once he laid out that Buffalo had short rest before a road game after beating a great Vikings defense in Minneapolis last Monday night.

"This is the best win we've had this season," Brady said, via the team's site.

"We're getting back real early Tuesday morning [from Minnesota] to be able to reset and get their bodies ready to go to go back on the road."

It absolutely was impressive for the Bills to win 31-12 in a letdown spot, no matter the competition. The Bills host the Dolphins this weekend before a big showdown against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving.

The Bengals' performance Sunday night might have been the most impressive of the NFL season . Critics doubted the Steelers' 6-2 start, but they ranked sixth in DVOA coming into Sunday night's game. And the Bengals made them look like a bottom-feeding Conference USA opponent in town for homecoming. The Bengals outgained the Steelers 337-40 in the first half, which shouldn't happen against any competent NFL team. Cincinnati looked like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. It now ranks No. 1 in DVOA this season.

Joe Burrow had 302 passing yards and three touchdowns by halftime. If the Steelers had kept it competitive, Burrow might have challenged Norm Van Brocklin's longstanding NFL record of 554 passing yards in a game. Burrow finished with 409 passing yards. When asked what kind of quarterback he was on Sunday night, Burrow said, "A great one." The Bengals are feeling good, and rightfully so. The biggest key might be the offensive line, which allowed one sack on 46 dropbacks from Burrow.

"They've been unbelievable," Burrow said, via the team's transcripts.

The Bears didn't do anything wrong on their bye week. They didn't "move down." The Bengals just moved up after one of the most impressive games of the season.

Lingering for the Bears is their home defeat to the Vikings in Week 2. They lost 9-3, and based on how the Vikings looked with Kirk Cousins in Week 10, that could be a problem . The Bears play at Minnesota in Week 18 and that's looking like an early candidate to be flexed to the final Sunday night slot.

Chicago is 0-2 in the division (Minnesota is 3-1) and that could also be bad for tiebreakers. The Lions suffered a massive injury to Aidan Hutchinson on Sunday and the Packers lost ground with a bad loss, so the NFC North could evolve into a two-team race. And the Bears might need to win in Minneapolis in Week 18 to take the division.

The Vikings blew out the Packers without three key players: linebacker Blake Cashman, receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson. Kirk Cousins is 38 and there should be skepticism whether he can turn the Vikings into a Super Bowl threat, but everything looked much better in Week 10. And receiver Justin Jefferson had a surprisingly self-aware comment on where the Vikings stand.

"All we as an offense have to do is be mediocre at this point," Jefferson said, via The Athletic . "The defense is creating so much pressure."

He's not wrong. The Vikings were fierce on Sunday, pressuring Jordan Love 22 times on 35 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus . Love was sacked eight times. The Vikings weren't tremendous on offense with 312 yards, but as Jefferson pointed out, that might be enough.

The Chiefs also didn't do anything to "move down" in a thorough 35-13 win over the Falcons . The Vikings needed to be adjusted after seeing them play well with Kirk Cousins. At this point it's fair to wonder if the Chiefs are being underrated, which is strange for a team that has been in the spotlight so much over the Patrick Mahomes era. There isn't much evidence to suggest they should be higher. They're eighth in DVOA. They're sixth in Super Bowl odds. They're sixth in offensive and defensive EPA. They're clearly good, but are they Super Bowl contender good?

A big piece of that answer could be Josh Downs. He had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown just five days after he was traded to the Chiefs. Xavier Worthy was shut out, and we can finally close the book on him making any meaningful impact. It's just not going to happen. The Chiefs need something extra in the offense, and perhaps it's Downs, who always seemed to have more potential and the Colts couldn't unlock it. Mahomes had 348 passing yards and five touchdowns on Sunday and perhaps that's a sign of a hot streak coming.

It's hard to find an advanced metric that indicates the Broncos should be higher than this. They're 14th in point differential, ninth in DVOA, 15th in net EPA as of last week and also a stunning 30th in yards per game on offense and 27th in yards allowed per game on defense. Their Super Bowl odds are tied for ninth best, for what that's worth. But here's why that doesn't matter: Denver is 7-2 after stacking (close) wins and has the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA, after playing the hardest schedule to this point in the season.

Here's what Denver has coming up: vs. Raiders, at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers. That's two playoff contenders (assuming Drake Maye's injury sinks the Patriots) of eight remaining games. Like last season, the Broncos could end up with 13 or 14 wins and an army of naysayers wondering how good they really are.

The Sam Darnold/Drew Lock debate is flawed. Lock's three starts came twice against the Cardinals and vs. the Raiders. Arizona and Las Vegas have two of the worst defenses in the NFL. Still, Lock has played well and Darnold has been prone to turnovers. Lock hasn't thrown an interception and Darnold has nine despite missing three games and almost all of a fourth. But there isn't any indication from Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald that he's considering a change.

"Drew's been fantastic," Macdonald said Monday on Seattle Sports 710, via the Seattle Times . "Drew's been phenomenal. But Sam's our quarterback."

That's the correct answer. Lock has played well and if Darnold continues to struggle, the Seahawks can turn to him later in the season. It would be premature to make a switch based on three games against bad opponents.

The Rams have won four in a row. They're still more likely than not to miss the playoffs — 44.2% chance to make it, via DVOA — because they have by far the NFL's toughest remaining schedule. But the Rams played well, albeit against a bad Cardinals team using rookie quarterback Carson Beck in his first career start. The Rams won 34-6 by running it 46 times for 202 yards. Konata Mumpfield provided some hope at receiver with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out, with three catches for 81 yards. L.A.'s defense limited Arizona to six first downs.

It's still a hard path to the playoffs because of the schedule and injuries, but the Rams are hanging around.

"I think it's really tested our team," head coach Sean McVay said of having to find injury replacements. "But it's also shown there's a lot of guys that are capable of, hey let's instill belief and then let's go have that confidence earned through evidence."

The Lions' season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson . They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That's brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they're nowhere near Hutchinson's level.

"Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he's a captain of ours — that doesn't make things easy," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com .

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

The Packers' bye comes at a good time. They were playing very well before Sunday, when they were crushed at home by the Vikings. The break gives the Packers a chance to regroup, and also perhaps get Micah Parsons back for a game against the Rams the day before Thanksgiving. The Packers should rightly believe that Parsons will transform their team upon his return.

But there are concerns after Sunday. The offensive line was in shambles against the Vikings after showing improvement over a few weeks. The Vikings are a tough matchup, but Jordan Love can't get hit 12 times. The running game also disappeared without Josh Jacobs as Green Bay had just 56 yards on 17 carries. There are some things to clean up before a massive game in the wild-card race against the Rams.

Was Sunday's outing just a bad night against a hot Bengals team or a bad sign for the Steelers going forward? It's OK to excuse it as a one-off. Before the 38-18 blowout loss, the Steelers were 6-2 and showing improvement. It's also OK to worry that Pittsburgh was exposed, though Aaron Rodgers didn't think so when asked if the loss changes the season's trajectory.

"That's very dramatic," Rodgers said, via the team's site . "I've been a part of this league for a long time. There's big wins, there's tough losses, so we'll deal with this properly."

One thing that is an issue for the Steelers is their receiver room. DK Metcalf continued to have minimal impact, as he was held without a catch before garbage time in the fourth quarter. Germie Bernard was blanked and has just 57 yards in Pittsburgh's last three games. No other healthy receiver on the roster has more than 39 yards this season. Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. could both return in the next couple weeks, and that is badly needed.

One developing story is what to do with Deshaun Watson. Those who log quarterback wins will say he is 6-3 this season. That's misguided, but many people follow that logic. Watson is 20th in adjusted EPA per play and he has a middling 89.1 passer rating. That's 20th among quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts. The Browns have had some fun comeback wins and it will be interesting to see if Cleveland overreacts to that and extends Watson, whose contract has been one of the worst in the NFL.

Certainly, the Browns would rather not have to come back and win every game, as they've been doing.

"I wish collectively him and I together would play better early and coach better early and we didn't have to get to this," Browns head coach Todd Monken said, via the team's transcripts. "And it's not just been them. It's been our team, last week the same way."

The Buccaneers looked to have a tough four-game stretch after the bye when the schedule came out. It has gotten much easier. Their next four opponents are the Lions (lost Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell to injuries between Weeks 8 and 10), Panthers (lost three in a row before a win Sunday), Chargers (a stunningly bad start to the season) and Ravens (lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries). That's why forecasting schedule strength can be difficult.

Now the Buccaneers have to take advantage of their good fortune. They're up to a 60.9% chance to win the division, via DVOA, in part because their defense ranks first in the NFL in that metric and they have the third-easiest remaining schedule.

The Giants are still in fine shape to win the NFC East because the Cowboys seem incapable of getting a stop on defense and the Commanders are flawed too. But blowing Thursday night's game against Washington keeps the pressure on them. The Giants had two chances to put the game away with the lead but went three-and-out each time. Then J.J. McCarthy threw an interception to end the game.

Otherwise, McCarthy played pretty well. He was 23-of-36 passing for 293 yards. Since Week 6, which was his first significant playing time with the Giants, he's 10th in adjusted EPA per play among quarterbacks with at least 100 plays. He hasn't been perfect but he's still young, and joining a team in-season and becoming a starter is a tough assignment.

"I thought he played very well," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the loss to the Commanders, according to the team's transcripts. "I mean, there were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well."

The Panthers paid edge rusher Jaelan Phillips $120 million over four years, and at that price point Phillips should be one of the biggest impact players in the NFL. On Sunday, he finally was. Phillips had three tackles for loss, including a sack, and the Panthers tied their season best by allowing 222 yards in a win over the Saints.

The Panthers' defense, along with a huge game from running back Chuba Hubbard, was the difference in a major victory in the NFC South race. It was Phillips' first game back after missing three due to a hamstring injury.

"Obviously there's been a lot of adversity, a lot of change, things happening, and we deserve some good things happening to us, so it was really good to get out there and play well." Phillips said, via the team's site .

Sunday was the fifth time this season that the Texans have given up a drive in the final minutes of regulation or overtime to lose a game. Houston was supposed to be one of the best defenses in the NFL. The Texans were second in EPA per play allowed last season. This season they're 20th, despite having mostly the same personnel and coaches.

While defensive success can fluctuate from season to season more than offensive success, the Texans' decline is perplexing. If Houston finished just two of those five games, it would be above .500.

"We have to play better — run defense, have to tackle better," head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire .

Fernando Mendoza made plenty of mistakes in his first NFL start, but he faced a Seattle defense that is among the top three in the NFL. Mendoza was 17-of-29 passing for 143 yards, and the biggest issue was that he took six sacks.

Mendoza will get better, though his next two matchups are also tough at Denver and at Cleveland. The schedule will get easier, but one of the concerns of the Kirk Cousins trade was shoving Mendoza into the lineup during a very difficult stretch. That was evident during a tough matchup against Seattle.

"It's good to get punched in the face, because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game, as a future hopeful leader of this offense," Mendoza said, via the Raiders' site .

20. Washington Commanders (3-5-1, LW: 24)

Linebacker Sonny Styles is going to make a case for Defensive Rookie of the Year. Against the Giants, the seventh overall pick of the draft had 13 tackles. His biggest tackle came on a third-and-3 right after the two-minute warning when he shot through for a tackle for loss on a J.J. McCarthy designed quarterback run. Styles read that play because the Giants had run it in Week 5, which is high-level awareness from a rookie.

That tackle allowed Washington to get the ball back, and Jayden Daniels led a game-winning drive that kept the Commanders' season alive. Styles is up to 80 tackles on the season and he is used often as a blitzer. He has one interception and one sack. He is looking like a great first-round pick.

The Patriots took a big drop in the rankings and it might not be far enough. Drake Maye suffered what the Patriots fear is a fractured ankle , per ESPN. At the very least he'll be out a while and the most likely outcome seems to be that his season is over.

That turns the offense over to Tommy DeVito. It has been a long time since he had a few decent games as a rookie for the Giants in 2023 and became a fleeting cult figure. He looked entirely overmatched Sunday after Maye left the game. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts against a bad Lions defense. It's hard to see how the Patriots keep their season afloat without Maye, unless DeVito somehow plays way better than he did Sunday or the Patriots find some very unexpected help off the street.

There's not much more that can be said about the Cowboys' defense. Even noted Cowboys fan Post Malone was absolutely fed up . After allowing 584 yards in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Brian Schottenheimer made perhaps his harshest comments on the team since becoming head coach.

"I thought the second half was unacceptable," Schottenheimer said, according to the team's site . "Tackling was atrocious. We're going to do a deep dive and see why."

It's not like the Cowboys' offense has been the 1999 Rams or anything: fifth in points scored, eighth in yards gained, fifth in EPA per play and sixth in DVOA. That still should be enough to win a poor division. The defense is ruining the Cowboys' season, though DVOA still gives Dallas a 32.4% chance to win the NFC East.

The Ravens lost but can't put all the blame on quarterback injuries. Jacoby Brissett had 340 yards and mostly played well. But the running game was invisible on Monday night against the Chargers. Derrick Henry had just 10 yards on 10 carries. Baltimore's defense wasn't good enough, allowing Los Angeles to rush for a season-best 160 yards. The Ravens have lost five in a row and are in a bad place the rest of the season.

The AFC wild-card race is soft, but it's not like the Ravens are looking like much of a threat. They just lost a home game to a Chargers team that was 0-8 coming in. Even if Lamar Jackson heals quickly, it seems like there won't be any reason for him to return late in the season.

The Saints' next three games are at Chicago, at Cincinnati and vs. Green Bay. This could get bad for New Orleans, which is showing that last season's strong second half was a fluke fueled by a weak schedule. The Panthers have allowed less than 300 yards this season four times: vs. the Cooper Rush-led Falcons, vs. the Browns, vs. the Tanner McKee-led Eagles and on Sunday against the Saints. New Orleans had just 222 yards of offense. There were offensive line injuries but it was still a poor performance and a bad home loss.

"Yeah, [coach Kellen Moore] was upset, and rightfully so," Saints quarterback Tyler Shough said via the team's transcripts. "As players, I think we failed him. As coach, I think we had those moments where we had a couple third downs, and I could have found Chris [Olave] or made a play there. We had those opportunities, and he's obviously frustrated. We have to find a way to win that game."

If there was a positive it was seeing a healthy Jordyn Tyson, the Saints' first-round draft pick, grab 11 passes for 80 yards as Carolina focused its coverage on Olave.

In Weeks 3 and 4, with Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup, the Falcons blew out the Packers and Saints and looked like a potential division winner. Other than those two games, the Falcons are 1-7. Whatever happened in those games was a complete outlier. Atlanta averaged 459 yards in those two games and hasn't been above 370 yards in any other game this season. Bijan Robinson hasn't rushed for more than 100 yards in a game since that Week 4 win at New Orleans.

On Sunday the defense completely let down, days after the team traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars. Patrick Mahomes had 348 yards and five touchdowns and Kansas City scored 35 points without running back Kenneth Walker III.

"All of this falls on me," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said, via the team's site . "So, I'll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better; that's the truth."

Everyone got way too excited for rookie quarterback Carson Beck because of one solid performance in the Hall of Fame Game. The overreaction to that was fierce. Beck, in his first game since then (he missed the rest of the preseason with a rib injury), had 108 yards and a 38.4 passer rating. Arizona had just six first downs and didn't score a touchdown. Beck had a tough matchup against the Rams and the Cardinals had many injuries on offense. Sunday was still a reality check. Beck could be a good player, but it's going to take time.

"It was a rough day, and that's probably a nice way of saying it, for the offense," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said, via the team's site , though he also said he "was impressed" with Beck.

The good news for Beck is the Cardinals aren't going anywhere and have no other option at quarterback the rest of the way. They'll get seven more games to evaluate Beck and he'll have some easier matchups. Arizona will know whether it has its quarterback for 2027 or needs to draft another one.

The Colts can win without their fans being conflicted because the team doesn't have its own 2027 first-round pick. Something that made no sense at the trade deadline and made less sense Sunday is why Indianapolis didn't deal away running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts had reported offers of a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor and they passed. Yet, the Colts split the backfield between Taylor and Seth McGowan again Sunday, with Taylor getting 16 carries and McGowan 12. The Colts could get a committee back for much cheaper than a second-round pick. As for the idea of not wearing out Taylor in a lost season, do they think they'll be a playoff contender next season? Seems unlikely.

The other part of the Colts' season that is hard to believe is how bad Daniel Jones has been. Jones had 108 yards and a 41.5 passer rating against a bad Dolphins defense. Jones has the lowest passer rating of any regular starting quarterback in the NFL this season, at 67. That's a 33-point drop from last season, which is stunning even accounting for injuries and trades.

Kyle McCord wasn't all that bad against the Colts in his first NFL start. He easily outplayed his counterpart, Daniel Jones. He was 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards and he ran for a touchdown. McCord also lost a fumble that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he was impressed with how McCord bounced back afterward.

"He didn't blink. He just stayed composed," Hafley said, according to the team's transcripts. "Coming out of the half, I mean, that thing could have gotten ugly and the game could have gotten away from us when he fumbled the ball and they scored, and he just kept responding the whole entire time."

McCord has at least a few more weeks to show what he can do in the NFL as Malik Willis is on injured reserve. With a little more improvement he can perhaps carve out a role as a reliable backup.

Cam Ward has improved, and Titans head coach Robert Saleh revealed Monday that the team gave Ward more responsibility at the line of scrimmage before Week 7. In the three games since, the Titans' scoring average has spiked from 14 points per game to 27.7, and that came against three good defenses (Browns, Bengals, Jaguars). Ward has three games this season with a passer rating above 83 and two of them came since the philosophical change.

The Titans are in the middle of a lost season, but a strong second half from Ward can offer renewed hope for the future.

"To be fair to Cam, we've said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans," Saleh said, via the team's site . "So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not he is capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it."

Not much has gone right for the Eagles this season, but the A.J. Brown trade looks to be a win for them. Brown has been stunningly bad for the Patriots. A high ankle sprain suffered in Week 1 has contributed to his quiet season. Overall, New England can't be happy to have just 11 catches and 128 yards from a receiver who will be 30 years old next season and cost the Patriots a 2028 first-round draft pick.

The Eagles are positioned well in the next two drafts, with extra first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and extra second-round picks in 2028 and 2029, because of the trades of Jordan Davis, Cam Jurgens and Brown. That might not make the rest of this season any more palatable but Philadelphia should be able to reload quickly.

When Aaron Glenn said he was taking over defensive play-calling this season, he said calling plays was his "superpower." On Sunday, he gave up the "lead" play-calling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, which practically means that Glenn is no longer the play-caller. Not that Jets fans needed another sign that Glenn won't be back in 2027 as New York's head coach, but that adds to the list.

The next big question will be when to flip the QB1 job to rookie Cade Klubnik from veteran Geno Smith. Klubnik got some playing time after Smith injured his ankle Sunday, and a 2-8 team should be thinking about getting a look at a rookie and benching a 36-year-old who will be a free agent after the season. Glenn said that's not a consideration yet.

"Geno's our starter," Glenn said Monday, via ESPN . "Come on now, let's not do that.

"I think Geno's had a really good year and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."

The Chargers got the win they needed to avoid a lot of annoying 0-17 questions. Let's not get too far ahead of ourselves; it was just one win, and on the whole, they've still been the NFL's worst team this season. But give the Chargers credit for a good effort. They figured out how to make the Ravens one-dimensional. Baltimore had 16 yards rushing on 15 carries. That forced Baltimore to lean too much on quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was making his first Ravens start after being traded less than two weeks ago.

It was also encouraging to see Omarion Hampton emerge with a 105-yard rushing day. Justin Herbert completed only 12 passes but he didn't need to do much more because the running game was effective. Maybe the Chargers can build on their first win and have a respectable second half of the season.

articles.title: Everything Justin Herbert Said After Chargers Snap Historic Losing Streak, Earn 1st Win of Season
articles.summary: It has been a season to forget for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers, but they finally got a win in their ninth try when they defeated the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday.
articles.body:
It has been a season to forget for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers, but they finally got a win in their ninth try when they defeated the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday.

"I just respect those guys in the locker room so much for sticking together, not pointing fingers," Herbert told ESPN after the win. "It's been a tough year, obviously, but the way they continue to show up to work, they're true professionals and I'm honored to be a part of it."

The victory snapped an 11-game losing streak dating back to last season and including the playoffs, which was tied for the longest in franchise history.

But Herbert explained the team has remained close in the face of adversity.

"It's a great locker room of guys," he said. "You know, guys that care about each other and want to be the best. It hasn't gone our way this year, but we're going to continue to show up to work tomorrow and watch the film and get better. And that's all we can do at this point."

Herbert had an unspectacular game through the air at 12-of-18 for 129 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions, but he added 51 yards on the ground. He also scored the game's opening touchdown using his legs when he broke free for a 22-yard score.

The story was the defense, though, which held Derrick Henry to a paltry 10 yards on 10 carries and forced two turnovers against a Baltimore offense playing with Jacoby Brissett under center for the first time after acquiring him via trade from the Arizona Cardinals.

While Brissett was less dangerous than a healthy Lamar Jackson, he still posed a challenge for the Chargers because of his ability to hit receivers downfield.

Yet the visitors prevented him from throwing for a single touchdown despite his 340 passing yards, which helped pave the way for the team's first win of the season.

articles.title: NFL: Baltimore Ravens beaten by Los Angeles Chargers to leave season on brink as Justin Herbert's side claim first win
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers end their losing 0-8 start to the season by beating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 behind Omarion Hampton's impressive efforts on the ground; the Ravens remain without quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is out for up to 10 weeks with a thumb injury
articles.body:
Derrick Henry was held to 10 yards on 10 carries, although he did score two touchdowns as Baltimore (4-6) skidded to its fifth straight loss and by far the most demoralising.

The Chargers (1-8) had lost 11 in a row dating back to last season but they outrushed the Ravens 160-16.

The combined 15 straight losses by the Chargers and Ravens entering the game was a record for a Monday night game.

Herbert completed only 12 passes for 129 yards, but his 22-yard scoring run on the first Los Angeles possession gave the Chargers a lead they wouldn't relinquish.

"I respect those guys in that locker room so much, for sticking together, not pointing fingers," said Herbert. "It's been a tough year, but the way they continue to show up to work, they're true professionals and I'm honoured to be part of it."

With the Chargers up 23-20, Baltimore's Zay Flowers lost a fumble after catching a pass near the Los Angeles 45 with 2:03 remaining.

Then Herbert threw to ex-Raven Charlie Kolar for the first down that all but ended the game.

Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Baltimore debut. With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve, the Ravens traded for Brissett in the hope that the veteran could at least keep the offense functional as Baltimore tries to avoid falling out of playoff contention.

The Ravens began the game by going three-and-out three straight times, and boos rained down on a Baltimore team that's now lost seven of its last eight home games - four at night - at a time when it was supposed to be competing for Super Bowls.

Brissett and the offense gradually improved. A two-yard touchdown run by Henry cut the Los Angeles lead to 10-7, but after an interception, Hampton produced one of the game's key plays.

On fourth down from the one, he was initially stopped by linebacker Roquan Smith, but Hampton was able to power into the end zone with some help from a couple of team-mates. That made it 17-7 with 1:56 left in the half.

Neither team reached the end zone again until Henry's one-yard run made it 23-20 with 10:23 left.

articles.title: Emmanuel Oyebadejo: Scouted as a spectator, now on brink of NFL
articles.summary: Emmanuel Oyebadejo was supposed to be studying medicine and playing basketball. How did he become tipped to make British history in a completely different sport?
articles.body:
When medical student Emmanuel Oyebadejo went to watch his friend's American football game, he had no idea he would end up being scouted himself for a sport he had never even played.

He wasn't even interested in it. In fact, while still at school in Manchester he'd delivered a speech titled 'I have a dream' in which he outlined plans to do "very well in basketball, return from the NBA and be the prime minister of the United Kingdom".

But now, four years later, he is being tipped to become the first Briton to be a first-round pick in the NFL Draft.

It is a rapid rise for the 22-year-old, who had to learn the game from scratch and win over his parents who "begged" him not to play and instead focus on his medical studies.

His biggest challenge at the start, though, was finding a pair of boots big enough for his size 16 feet.

It was 6ft 6in Oyebadejo's physique that had caught the eye of the coaching staff at Exeter Demons when he was a spectator for his friend's university game that was taking place at the club's home ground, The Crumb.

"I was talking to one of the other coaches, Jack Mullins, and we sort of turned around [and thought] 'that guy's freaking huge! We should go talk to him'," Lydon Ward-Best, one of the Demons' coaches, tells BBC Sport.

Oyebadejo had been a talented basketball player, playing for Manchester Magic - one of England's top junior clubs - from the age of 11 to 18. But by the time he was at the University of Exeter he was no longer playing competitively.

Lydon Ward-Best persuaded him to give a new sport a go.

"He started coming to training and just had the most ridiculous intro to American football I think I've ever seen," the coach adds.

A straight-A pupil, who had also learned the piano, guitar and drums while studying medicine, Oyebadejo had always been a quick learner.

"I always say that American football is kind of like violent chess," says Mullins, the Demons' current head coach.

"[Emmanuel] got the violent bit pretty quickly. He was fine at that - 'I am much bigger than you, watch me go'.

"The chess bit took a little longer because there's all these things that you have to think about."

But as Ward-Best puts it, "he's not just a big sort of jock athlete, he's a smart guy. He is so dedicated and disciplined with everything."

Oyebadejo played for the Demons at the end of the 2022-23 season, before the team went unbeaten in his first full season, 2023-24. When back home he also played for the Manchester Titans and helped them win the Britbowl in September 2023.

By December 2023, he decided he wanted to take things further. Could he make it in the United States? Would college teams be interested if he sent them videos of his highlights?

Coach Ward-Best told Oyebadejo it would be "tough", adding: "You know the percentages are not on your side here, but you are 6ft 6in and 280 pounds (20 stone), so you've got a better chance than most.

"I wanted to be realistic with him," he adds. "But I said I'd do whatever I could to help get him out there."

Emmanuel's father Oladini says he thought it was a "joke" and that he did not support him playing this "dangerous" game, explaining: "He had never played this game before. He'd only done it for a few months, so why would anybody from America want him?"

There was interest from several colleges and Oyebadejo ended up at Jacksonville State, where he would study biology and play under legendary college coach Rich Rodriguez, having managed to win his parents round thanks to the influence of an uncle who lived in Dallas and understood the sport.

His first season was hit by injury but, despite coming up against players who have played American football since they were young children, his second was a big success.

As a defensive end, Oyebadejo's job is to get past the offensive linemen trying to block him and tackle the ball carrier or claim a sack - when a defensive player tackles the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage.

He recorded 4.5 sacks, forced two fumbles and had 41 total tackles during the 2025 season.

Now the big college teams were paying attention.

College football is America's most passionate sporting pastime. While the NFL plays on Sundays, the college game dominates Saturdays during the autumn months.

And Oyebadejo transferred to the University of Florida to play for one of college football's biggest teams in the most prestigious conference, the Southeastern (SEC).

The Florida Gators are three-time national champions, have about 50 former players currently in the NFL and get home crowds of 90,000 at 'The Swamp'.

Oyebadejo was undaunted as he burst on to the scene. He had 2.5 sacks in a win at rivals Auburn in September and followed that up by impressing in big wins over Mississippi and Texas, the latter in front of 103,989 people.

After barely being on the radar of NFL scouts at the start of the season, Oyebadejo's form has propelled him into contention to be an early-round draft pick in 2027.

NFL teams do not have youth systems or academies. Almost all players have come through the US college system and they are recruited via the NFL Draft when they graduate.

One of the biggest events in the American sporting calendar, the NFL Draft takes place over three days in April, with the 32 teams taking turns to select players across seven rounds.

First-round picks in April will be guaranteed a rookie contract of at least $19.1m (£14.4m) and they are often fast-tracked into starting roles. The contract values decrease in a sliding scale so, for example, a third-round pick (top 96) will be guaranteed $7.3m (£5.5m).

Among the latest prospects, ESPN's veteran draft analyst Mel Kiper has ranked Oyebadejo as the fifth-best edge rusher (defensive end). That is regarded as the sport's second-most important position behind quarterback - and therefore the second-best paid in the NFL.

The reason is that Oyebadejo has everything needed to be a starting defensive end in the NFL. Firstly, his height and weight are ideally suited for the grappling battle required in what is known as 'the trenches'.

He has very long arms (7ft wingspan), perfect for winning a wrestling match against the kind of enormous opponent he faces, and unusually for a man as big as him, he's extremely quick. That's the money-making trait.

Although he now weighs about 300lbs (more than 21 stone), it is believed he has a remarkable body-fat percentage of about 12%. All his measurables are seen as ideal for a defensive end, if not better.

There are simply very few people with Oyebadejo's physical talent, and given the fast-tracked nature of his rise in American football, he does not look as raw as you might expect.

"He's British and has only played the sport for three [full] seasons," says his mentor and former coach Ward-Best. "You'd therefore think he must be very green, but he doesn't look that way.

"The physical qualities are clearly there but he's worked a lot on mastering aspects of the position as well."

Menelik Watson, also from Manchester, holds the record for being the highest-drafted British player. He was the 42nd pick in 2013 and spent six years in the NFL, earning a total of $16.4m (£13.7m).

London-born Osi Umenyiora, the 56th pick in 2003, enjoyed an illustrious 12-year career - winning two Super Bowls with the New York Giants.

"I have spoken to Osi, he's a really cool guy," says Oyebadejo, who is also of Nigerian heritage.

"To be a first-round pick out of the UK, it would be amazing. It would do so much for the American football community back home."

Oyebadejo impressed again in an upset win at Kentucky on Saturday and has 4.5 sacks with two regular-season games left. Florida could then play in a 'bowl' game, an end-of-season exhibition.

After that, Oyebadejo is expected to participate in a physical-testing event called the 'scouting combine', where he will be assessed by representatives of all 32 teams in March.

The draft then begins in Washington DC on 27 April, and if Oyebadejo hears his name called, he will complete an unlikely journey and make his now fully supportive parents very proud.

"It's mad," says Ward-Best. "I've been doing this for 20 years and I've never seen anything like this. We almost have to pinch ourselves."

Oyebadejo has stayed in touch with his former coaches in Exeter. The Demons hold watch parties for Florida games and there is a real sense of pride over where his journey began.

"It was just complete chance that he wanted to wander up to The Crumb and watch a game, just being there for his mate," says coach Mullins.

"If those things didn't happen, we wouldn't be having this conversation. He would be four years into his medical degree."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes worried about sore arm then threw 5 TDs; 49ers' Rocky Mountain high; Jordan Love hates sacks
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes admits he was nervous about his sore elbow, then silenced the doubts with 348 yards and five touchdown passes for Kansas City.
articles.body: Nobody asked Andy Reid about Patrick Mahomes, or the quarterback's health, or his elbow on Monday. The Kansas City Chiefs coach spoke with reporters at his usual day-after news conference and the troubled elbow on the team's golden-armed quarterback was not at all a topic of conversation. That felt strange because last week was all about Mahomes and his sore elbow. There was even concern, within the Kansas City organization, about whether Mahomes would be able to throw the football as effectively following an injury the week before. PATRICK MAHOMES SUFFERS APPARENT ELBOW INJURY ON THROWING ARM BUT RETURNS TO FACE NEW YORK JETS We know this is true because the concern was from the man himself. "I was a little nervous going into the game, just because it was a little sore," Mahomes admitted on Sunday. All that concern appeared serious. But then the star quarterback threw for 348 yards against the Atlanta Falcons. And he threw five touchdown passes. And his passer rating was 135.5. It was a performance that, evidently, soothed the fears Mahomes admitted he quietly felt before the game. "I didn’t feel like during the week of practice, I was driving the ball the way I wanted to," Mahomes confessed. "Just because of some of those deeper in-cut routes and the different balls down the field, you don’t know until you get out there and that adrenaline starts kicking a little bit. "And obviously, it was good enough." Mahomes playing as he did when his throwing arm was not 100%, with his mind questioning how effective he could be and without starting running back Kenneth Walker in the lineup, was impressive. KENNETH WALKER III OUT AGAINST NFL RUSHING LEADER BIJAN ROBINSON'S FALCONS, PATRICK MAHOMES OFF INJURY REPORT And this is where we have to acknowledge one of the things that makes Mahomes so great: His durability. In a league that mangles quarterbacks through the injury mill with alarming regularity — Lamar Jackson, Jaxson Dart, Sam Darnold, Drake Maye and Malik Willis so far this season – Mahomes is an iron man. He has delivered double-digit starts in each of his seasons dating back to 2018, when he first became Kansas City's starter. In some of those seasons, Mahomes was actually kept out of the lineup late in the season to save him for the playoffs. That durability has helped keep the Chiefs on a consistent championship arc when teams like the Bengals couldn't do the same with Joe Burrow and Baltimore couldn't do it with Jackson. His durability is a gift that keeps Mahomes among the best in the NFL. 49ers know things about acclimating Somebody in the Minnesota Vikings organization should be really questioning plans to stay in town this week ahead of Sunday night's game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City's Estadio Azteca. The venue is 7,350 feet above sea level, meaning the lung capacity of players and their ability to function high above sea level will be tested during the game. (By the way, I've covered a game at Estadio Azteca before and discovered my ability to eat the free halftime hot dog in the open-air press seating was not at all affected by the high altitude). But the 49ers are spending this week in Colorado Springs, which is some 6,035 feet above sea level, because coach Kyle Shanahan believes altitude acclimation will help his team, should give the Vikings pause. "I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me," Shanahan said. "No matter how good of shape you’re in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you’re out of breath. "It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it’s always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver." So why should the Vikings be second-guessing themselves now? Well ... because they've decided to stay at their practice facility this week before going to Mexico City. Club sources say they have other ways of acclimating. That's fine. But if you'll recall, way back in September, the 49ers traveled to Australia nearly a week before the game to acclimate to the time difference. The Rams arrived about 26 hours before the game. San Francisco 27. Los Angeles 7. Rams coach Sean McVay didn't stop second-guessing his travel plans for weeks. Hear that Minnesota Vikings? Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said the process of acclimating for this game "started weeks ago" to "best handle the short amount of time we're going to be there." This sounds like an advantage for the 49ers. Jordan Love hated everything about eight sacks Jordan Love was understandably a little hot after the Minnesota Vikings sacked him eight times on Sunday. This just in: Quarterbacks do not like to get hit. And Love responded by criticizing his offensive line. And his coaches. And himself. This was Love's takedown of everyone after he suffered an inglorious amount of takedowns on himself: "We have to do a better job identifying who's coming, you know, who we're sliding to, and doing a better job of picking some of that stuff up," Love said. "Because, like I said, it's not like they did anything we haven't seen on film. "So we just got to, we got to handle that stuff better. And I feel like they just kept bringing some similar stuff, and we didn't pick it up well enough." That took down the pass protection. Next? CRAIG CARTON CALLS OUT AIDAN HUTCHINSON FOR SELFISH SACK CELEBRATION - LISTEN NOW "It's not all just the line," Love said. "Like, we got to have better concepts to be able to get those balls out quicker." Coaches ripped? Check. "And I got do a better job of finding where I can go with the ball to get it out quicker to beat some of that stuff," he said in some solid self-flagellation. I love carpet-bombing Jordan Love. Quick off the ball with the twitch to generate movement when he establishes leverage, including flashes of lift and displacement against shaded defenders.

Lighter build and only adequate play-strength create problems against bigger interior defenders, who can stack him at first contact or knock him off his base when he cannot win leverage early.

Forward lean and inconsistent contact balance lead to too many reps on the ground, particularly when his initial leverage is compromised.

Pass-pro spacing can become loose, creating unnecessary interior room and forcing him to recover rather than maintaining tighter control from the start.

Trevor Goosby projects as a starting-caliber tackle with appealing physical tools, though his lower-body mechanics and range against NFL speed keep him just below first-round territory through the current evaluation. The junior prospect is a long-framed tackle with strong hands, a sturdy anchor and enough length to protect the corner when his set stays controlled. His size and play-strength allow him to absorb power and generate displacement in the run game, but his high-cut build creates noticeable stiffness when he has to redirect, recover or sustain leverage through movement.

Goosby is a 6'7", 325-pound tackle prospect who entered the Texas program as a 3-star recruit in the 2023 class.

The underclassman appeared in 17 games with two starts over his first two seasons before becoming a full-time starter. He earned first-team All-SEC honors from the league's coaches in 2025 and entered 2026 with 15 career starts before starting the first three games of his senior season at left tackle.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Massive frame with very good length and grip-strength to widen the corner, stay attached and wall rushers away from the quarterback when he reaches his set point.

Stout anchor when his base is underneath him, with the size and hand-strength to absorb speed-to-power without consistently conceding the depth of the pocket.

Generates force in the run game with strong hands and upper-body strength, particularly when he wins off the snap and can square up backside cutoffs or down blocks.

Uses his length to survive imperfect reps and recover late, giving him a larger margin for error than his lower-body quickness alone would provide.

High-cut frame creates stiffness and lag when redirecting against counters, with his upper and lower halves becoming disconnected and leading to overextension or loss of balance.

Edge range is more functional than dynamic against wide alignments; can become cornered when rushers threaten speed before working through or across his frame.

Leverage and sustain fluctuate in the run game, where defenders can stand him up, pull him through or shed across his face when his feet stop accompanying his hands.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Massive, long-armed starting tackle whose size, grip and anchor offset average redirect quickness

High-end play strength with the ability to generate lift, torque defenders out of gaps and create substantial vertical or lateral displacement once he gets his hips and hands connected.

Strong grip and hand strength allow him to latch, refit and sustain control through contact, with several reps where he transitions cleanly from the initial fit into a powerful drive phase.

Sturdy anchor against direct power, particularly when he stays square and keeps his feet underneath him. His center tape has produced some of his cleanest examples of absorbing force without unnecessary pocket concession.

Versatile run blocker with useful reach ability, combination-block timing and enough movement to climb and create displacement against linebackers. The Washington tape added several strong examples from center.

Body control is the defining concern. His upper body repeatedly gets ahead of his feet, leaving him vulnerable to push-pulls, sheds and sudden changes of direction after initially securing the block.

Sustain consistency does not match his play-strength, as defenders can work free late when his base narrows, his hips drift or he begins leaning into contact.

Can be late redirecting his feet against quick cross-face movement or second-level targets, forcing him into compromised recovery positions despite having enough strength to salvage some reps.

articles.title: Kyle Hamilton Says Ravens Are 'Disgracing the Standard' in New Video After Loss to Winless Chargers
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton didn't hide his frustration following the team's 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who entered 0-8 this season, on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton didn't hide his frustration following the team's 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who entered 0-8 this season, on Monday Night Football.

Speaking to reporters after the defeat, Hamilton said the Ravens are "disgracing the standard" amid their current five-game losing streak.

Chargers Post Dillon Brooks Laughing at LeBron Meme to Troll NFL Analysts All Picking Ravens to Win

Monday's result feels like the nadir of a season that is rapidly slipping away from the Ravens. Their issues were on both sides of the ball.

The Chargers tied their season-high with 23 points scored and ran for a season-high 160 yards on the ground. The latter stat is the most allowed by Baltimore's defense since Week 5 last season against the Houston Texans (167 yards).

Baltimore's offense had no balance between the run and pass whatsoever. Derrick Henry ran for 10 yards on 10 carries, though he did score two touchdowns. The Ravens' had a total of 16 rushing yards on 15 carries.

Jacoby Brissett, making his first start after being acquired in a Nov. 6 trade with the Arizona Cardinals, played well considering he had just over one week to learn the offense. He finished 33-of-49 for 340 yards and one interception.

The Ravens had a chance to take the lead late in the game, but a Zay Flowers fumble after a 15-yard reception was recovered by the Chargers with 2:03 remaining.

Los Angeles was able to run the clock down to 18 seconds before punting the ball back to the Ravens and a Hail Mary attempt from Brissett as time expired fell incomplete.

Trading for Brissett was supposed to stabilize things on offense enough to get by during a soft part of the schedule that would allow them to stick around in the playoff race with the hope Lamar Jackson could return late in the year.

In the aftermath of losing to the Chargers, the bottom appears to have fallen out in Baltimore. This is the Ravens' first losing streak of at least five games since 2021 when they lost their final six games after Jackson suffered an ankle injury in Week 14.

The Ravens' 4-6 record has them two games out of the final playoff spot in the AFC currently held by the Cleveland Browns.

Head coach Jesse Minter will look to right the ship for the Ravens on a short week when they travel to Bank of America Stadium for a matchup with the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

articles.title: 7 major NFL injury updates entering Week 11: Drake Maye, Brock Bowers & more
articles.summary: The latest updates on 7 big name players entering Week 11.
articles.body:
The NFL is heading into Week 11 with several notable injury situations to monitor, including questions surrounding starting quarterbacks, star pass catchers and key defensive players. With teams preparing for another week of action, Monday brought important updates on Drake Maye, Brock Bowers, Aidan Hutchinson and several others. Here is the latest on seven players as the Week 11 schedule approaches.

Drake Maye, Brock Bowers and Aidan Hutchinson injury updates

Drake Maye, Patriots QB (ankle): Head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he did not have an updated diagnosis for Maye, though he confirmed the quarterback is expected to miss time. "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said. New England will have to prepare for an extended absence from its starting quarterback.

Brock Bowers, Raiders TE (ankle): Bowers underwent additional testing Monday after failing to finish Sunday's game against the Seahawks. However, the initial belief is that he did not suffer a major ankle injury. He is considered day-to-day, with further testing expected to provide a clearer picture of his availability.

Aidan Hutchinson, Lions DE (knee): Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL against the Patriots. There is also concern about additional damage to his knee, making this a devastating loss for Detroit's defense.

More notable NFL injury updates entering Week 11

Luther Burden, Bears WR (concussion): Burden suited up and participated in Monday's practice session, an encouraging development as he works through the concussion situation.

Micah Parsons, Packers DE (knee): Parsons still has "a couple more hurdles to clear" before returning to the field, according to head coach Matt LaFleur. His availability for Week 11 remains uncertain.

Drake London, Falcons WR (concussion): London was evaluated for a concussion but cleared, according to head coach Kevin Stefanski. That is an encouraging update for Atlanta's passing attack.

Sam Darnold, Seahawks QB (quadriceps): Darnold is expected to get a full week of practice following Seattle's Week 11 bye. Head coach Mike Macdonald expects him to return to the starting role for the team's next game on November 29 against the San Francisco 49ers.
